doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

chapter: After the war: radio and road
title: Radio work with Abe Burrows and Milton DeLugg's band
summary: He worked around town with Savitt and Jerry Wald, then on Abe Burrows's radio show with DeLugg's difficult arrangements.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: So did you end up doing the radio thing?

Oh, so then I worked a little around town with Savitt, and worked with Jerry Wald I remember, Trocadero’s, you know places around town. I’m trying to think when I got the Judy Canova’s show. No the first one was Abe Burrows. Do you remember him?

Oh he’s famous as a musical comedy script writer. But he wasn’t then, but he was like a writer for whatever. And well you have to know who he was. He was a funny guy. He used to write these funny songs, and he would entertain at parties, and he got so famous
doing that that they hired him to do a radio show with these funny songs he used to write. But it was a good little band, Milton DeLugg — does that name ring a bell?

It was his band, just a little group about five, six. And he wrote these real complex arrangements. We only — maybe one number we had, but it was really hard, and you had to really read it and we’d go in and rehearse and then we’d have like about two or three hours off before the show. I remember I’d come back to the show it was like I’d never seen this music before.
And it was live of course, right?

Yeah. There were two broadcasts I think, I’m pretty sure, or I think they had tape by those days. You know they had an east coast broadcast and a west coast broadcast. We didn’t talk about the Tommy Dorsey—
